title: Election 2026 live updates: Democrats flip first Senate seat with Roy Cooper in North Carolina
text:
Election results 2026 live updates: Democrats flip early Senate and governor races 
 LIVE COVERAGE Updated now Election 2026 live updates: Texas and South Carolina Senate races lean toward Democrats
 Both parties are battling for control of Congress and in key governor’s races. NBC News Exit Polls show an electorate that disapproves of the job Congress and the president are doing.
 Save Add NBC News to Google Updated November 03, 2026, 9:35 PM EST By NBC News What to know on Election Day 
 SENATE FLIP: Democrats have flipped the first Senate seat of the night in North Carolina, the NBC News Decision Desk projects. The party has also notched wins in two other battlegrounds, Georgia and New Hampshire . Senate battleground races in Texas, Ohio and South Carolina lean toward Democrats .
 GOVERNOR RACES: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms has won the governor's race in Georgia , while Republican Rep. Byron Donalds will be Florida's next governor , NBC News projects. Both will be the first Black governors of their states. Bottoms' win is a flip for Democrats.
 POLLS CLOSE: Polls have closed in more than half the country and results are rolling in. Recent polling suggests Democrats are in a strong position to retake the House, while the Senate majority could come down to competitive races in traditionally red states.
 NBC NEWS EXIT POLLS: Early results from the NBC News Exit Polls show a dissatisfied electorate, with President Donald Trump’s disapproval rating at a dismal 62% and more than three-quarters of voters saying they disapprove of the job Congress is doing, as well. Nearly half of voters say they view the election as an opportunity to rebuke Trump.
 KORNACKI: Steve is live at the big board. Check out his latest Data Dive newsletter , for a look at the handful of races that could set the tone tonight.
 ELECTION RESULTS: Follow along this evening for results, detailed election data , analysis and on-the-ground reporting from correspondents across the country. NBC News primetime coverage will be going all night. 
 NEW UPDATES Just now San Diego election officials rebuff accusations of ballot box irregularities 
 San Diego County officials and a Republican watchdog group say voting has proceeded smoothly there, after a video shared on social media spurred rumors that some ballots had been handled inappropriately. 
 The video, posted by an account belonging to Amy Reichert, a former county board of supervisor candidate, appeared to show poll workers wearing county Registrar of Voters vests collecting ballots from an overflowing dropoff location outside a library. One of the poll workers can be seen saying that he and his colleagues were preparing to take the ballots to the Registrar of Voters to be tallied.
 In the video, a poll worker tells a handful of voters gathered around that the ballot box got so full that it jammed. The location had to stop accepting ballots temporarily, the worker says, suggesting that voters bring their ballots to alternative locations.
 The person who filmed the video said they stuck around until the ballot box started accepting ballots again. The voter requested that their name not be published for fear of political blowback.
 Show more The video gained traction after Reichert crossposted it on Instagram, Facebook and Twitter, with some users suggesting that election workers might have been stealing or discarding the ballots. 
 In a separate social media post, Reichert shared a photo of a grey truck with out-of-state plates and said that a “witness” had seen the ballots being loaded onto the truck.
 The X account @RNCVoteProtect, an electoral watchdog wing of the GOP, said the group had looked into the issue and did not find any irregularities. 
 A spokesperson for San Diego County said the video showed election workers doing what they were hired to do: collect ballots. 
 “The video in question shows ballot collection in action. Voted ballots are being collected and returned securely to the Registrar of Voters office in accordance with established chain-of-custody procedures,” Antonia Hutzell, with the County of San Diego Registrar of Voters, said in a statement to NBC News. 
 “We can confirm that there are no issues with ballot collection or election operations.”
 Hutzell added that ballot boxes at some dropoff locations filled up more quickly than others, which is why the workers were seen picking up ballots in the morning. The Registrar regularly uses rental vehicles as part of its fleet, she said. 
 “Election officials maintain established chain-of-custody, ballot security and collection procedures for all ballots returned by voters,” Hutzell said. “Voting and ballot processing operations continue as normal.”
 In response to the explanation from the Registrar of Voters, Reichart said: “People take the time to carefully fill out their ballots, trusting that when they place them in an official ballot drop box, they’ll be handled securely.”
 Just now NBC News Decision Desk: Texas Senate race leans toward Democrats 
 The Texas Senate race leans toward Democrat James Talarico. This indicates NBC News is at least 75% confident in the outcome of this race.
 2m ago / 9:33 PM EST Long lines at the polls? Free pizza to the rescue. 
 The sun has set over Los Angeles County, and the line to vote at Langley Senior Center in Monterey Park stretches around the block. 
 Priscilla Lopez said it took an hour for her to vote. But she was willing to wait even longer — this time for eight pizzas to arrive from “Pizza to the Polls.”
 “I heard about them on TikTok,” said the 35 year old healthcare worker. 
 According to its website, the nonprofit promises to deliver free pizzas to everyone waiting to vote for over an hour. 
 Show more Minutes later, a delivery worker arrived with eight cheese pizzas. Lopez handed them out to election volunteers and dozens of people waiting in line to vote. 
 Annie Nguyen, 72, was the first to grab a slice — after waiting over an hour in line. “With older people like me, they need to let them go separately because I waited here so long,” she said. 
 Eighteen-year-old Brianna Evans grabbed a slice at the back of the line. “I’m here for as long as it takes,” she said. “I just want what’s best for California — what’s best for my future.”
 2m ago / 9:32 PM EST NBC News Exit Poll in Florida: Byron Donalds wins governor's race with support from conservative and rural voters 
 Republican Byron Donalds prevailed over Democrat David Jolly to become the first Black governor of Florida, NBC News projects. Republican and conservative voters solidly backed Donalds’ candidacy, according to the NBC News Exit Poll .
 In addition, 61% of small town and rural voters supported Donalds, as well as more than half of white voters (58%) and voters age 45 and older (55%). It’s notable, however, that Black voters in Florida backed Jolly 87% to 13% for Donalds.
 9m ago / 9:26 PM EST NBC News Decision Desk: South Carolina Senate race leans toward Democrats 
 The South Carolina Senate race leans toward Democrat Annie Andrews. This indicates NBC News is at least 75% confident in the outcome of this race.
 10m ago / 9:24 PM EST A record number of Black governors will serve concurrently next year 
 With GOP Rep. Byron Donalds projected to win Florida's governor's race and former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms projected to win Georgia's governor's race, there will be a record number of Black governors serving in the U.S. next year.
 Lance Bottoms and Donalds will join Maryland Gov. Wes Moore, who is projected to win re-election tonight, as the second and third Black governors in office.
 Byron Donalds, Keisha Lance Bottoms and Wes Moore.   WireImage; Getty 
 Previously, only two Black governors served at once. Lance Bottoms also made history tonight by being the first female Black governor elected in the U.S.
 There are several other Black candidates for governor on the ballot tonight who could raise the record number of Black state executives if they are projected to win later. Those include David Crowley in Wisconsin, John James in Michigan, Aaron Ford in Nevada, Lisa Demuth in Minnesota and Jermaine Johnson in South Carolina.
 10m ago / 9:24 PM EST Democrat Vicente Gonzalez wins re-election in Texas's 34th Congressional District, NBC News projects 
 Democrat Rep. Vicente Gonzalez has defeated Republican Eric Flores to win another term in Texas's 34th Congressional District, NBC News projects.

 15m ago / 9:20 PM EST Sen. Darline Graham's lead lags behind Trump's 2024 success in her South Carolina home county 
 Sen. Darline Graham has a comfortable lead in her home county, though her margin over Democrat Annie Andrews is significantly smaller than Trump's over Kamala Harris in 2024. 
 With 92% of the vote counted, Graham has a 29-point lead over Andrews in Pickens County, where she and her late brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham, were born. 
 Trump won that same county by 53 points in 2024. 
 15m ago / 9:19 PM EST Democrat Penny Reynolds wins Georgia secretary of state 
 Democrat Penny Reynolds has won the Georgia Secretary of State race, NBC News has projected.
 Judge Penny Brown Reynolds, a Democrat known for a family court television show and serving in the Biden administration, ran against Trump-endorsed state Rep. Tim Fleming, a former aide to outgoing Republican Gov. Brian Kemp.
 Fleming called for more mail voting restrictions and said there were "irregularities" in the 2020 election, while Reynolds campaigned as a judge who would stand up to Trump while following the law in running state elections.
 The state is a critical battleground ahead of the 2028 presidential election and a key target for Democrats .
 Judge Penny Brown Reynolds on Monday in Decatur, Ga.   Megan Varner / Getty Images 
 16m ago / 9:19 PM EST Republican Andy Barr wins the Kentucky Senate race, NBC News projects 
 Republican Andy Barr has defeated Democrat Charles Booker in the Kentucky Senate race, NBC News projects.
 See the latest results here. 
 17m ago / 9:18 PM EST Keisha Lance Bottoms' results in Georgia governor's race reveals dynamics at play in battleground state 
 There’s an interesting dynamic to think about in Georgia when it comes to Republicans, as we think about Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms' victory in the governor’s race.
 The most popular Republican is Brian Kemp, the former governor, who the GOP tried to convince to run for Senate, but he chose not to. Then they turned away his pick for Senate, the former football coach Derek Dooley. Trump was the person behind that decision not to get behind Dooley. Again, this trend line continues of President Trump inserting himself into these races and trying to pick the candidates, and then that backfiring on the candidates in question.
 Meanwhile, there are real 2028 implications with the Lance Bottoms result. Georgia is obviously one of the most important battleground states in a presidential race. And if it is starting to shift bluer, that could be a good sign for Democrats in two years. And by the way, we’re keeping the focus on 2026 but throwing it out there: If re-elected Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff decided to run for president in 2028, it would be a Democratic governor who’d pick his replacement.
 Keisha Lance Bottoms on Tuesday in Smyrna, Ga.   Brynn Anderson / AP 
 18m ago / 9:17 PM EST NBC News Exit Poll in Maine: Susan Collins may be in jeopardy as she loses young and independent voters 
 Sen. Susan Collins' remarkable run as the longest-serving Republican woman in Senate history may be in jeopardy as she loses support among young voters and independents, according to early results from the NBC News Exit Poll . 
 Earlier in her career, Collins routinely bested her opponents among voters under age 30. As recently as 2014, she won two-thirds of their vote.
 This dynamic changed during the Trump era, however. Her support with young voters dropped noticeably in 2020 and sank even further this year to 25%, according to the NBC News Exit Poll. One reason appears to be Trump. Close to two-thirds (64%) of Maine voters under age 30 say Collins is too supportive of Trump.
 Historically, part of Collins’ recipe for success was her deep connection with Maine’s independent-minded electorate. Dating back to her first Senate victory in 1996, she performed well among Maine voters who did not identify as Republicans or Democrats. However, this year Collins also appears to have lost independent voters. 
 But when it came to which candidate would bring home more federal funding, voters were nearly twice as likely to say Collins over Democratic challenger Troy Jackson (57% to 29%). As chair of the powerful Senate Appropriations Committee, Collins steered funding for community centers, railroad improvement projects and shipyards.
 Maine voters also expressed some reservations about Jackson. A slight majority of voters (56%) said he does not have the temperament to serve as a U.S. senator.
 23m ago / 9:12 PM EST Loss by Republican Rick Jackson in Georgia governor's race takes toll on his pocketbook 
 The loss by Georgia Republican gubernatorial hopeful Rick Jackson took quite a toll on his pocketbook. 
 Jackson spent more than $200 million on ads in his race, which NBC News projects he lost to Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms. 
 Jackson won a runoff contest against Trump-backed Lt. Gov. Burt Jones. 
 25m ago / 9:10 PM EST Competitive House seats are swinging to the left of Trump 
 It’s not just about flipping seats, it’s about looking at the margins.
 Of the 12 House seats the NBC News Decision Desk rated as competitive (meaning not safe for either party), seven are currently posting margins that represent at least a 10-point swing away from Republicans when compared to Trump’s 2024 margins there. The other five are still swinging to the left from Trump’s margin by at least 8 points.

 28m ago / 9:06 PM EST Minnesota voters remember Renee Good and Alex Pretti 
 On a rainy Election Day in Minneapolis, voters adorned the makeshift memorials dedicated to Renée Good and Alex Pretti with hundreds of “I Voted” stickers. 
 Good and Pretti were fatally shot in January by federal immigration agents while protesting against the Trump administration’s “Operation Metro Surge.”
 “I was at each memorial for about 15 minutes," said Darnell Edwards, who witnessed the somber tribute. "There was a constant stream of people, I would say four to five at a time. They would nod and pull their sticker out, place it and then leave. It was a heavy feeling.”
 Trump’s immigration crackdown has emerged as a key issue during the midterm elections. Most voters responding to the latest NBC News exit poll said Trump’s immigration enforcement actions have gone too far.
 Bridget Bennett / MinnPost / CatchLight via Getty 
 Bridget Bennett / MinnPost / CatchLight via Getty 
 31m ago / 9:04 PM EST Keisha Lance Bottoms wins the Georgia governor’s race, flipping the office for Democrats, NBC News projects 
 Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms projected to win Georgia governor's race 02:46 
 Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms has won Georgia’s race for governor, NBC News projects, defeating Republican Rick Jackson and flipping control of the battleground state office for the first time in 24 years.
 Bottoms, the former mayor of Atlanta and a former Biden administration official, overcame an enormous spending disadvantage against Jackson , a wealthy healthcare executive who pumped more than $100 million of his own money into his campaign.
 Read the full story here. 
 See the latest results here. 
 33m ago / 9:01 PM EST Maine women are swinging more toward Democrat Troy Jackson than they did for Susan Collins in 2020 
 Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, is a survivor; she's spent nearly three decades in the upper chamber. While Maine doesn’t count its votes all that quickly, women so far are swinging more toward Democrat Troy Jackson than they did for Collins six years ago.
 In 2020, Collins was up by 3 points with women in the exit polls. Jackson is up by 10 with women. This is a key constituency and demographic in that state — and a number that the Jackson campaign would want to be seeing right now.
 Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, faced off against Democrat Troy Jackson.   Getty 
 33m ago / 9:01 PM EST In Tarrant County, Texas, a long line of would-be voters wait in line as poll close looms 
 The line of people waiting to vote at the Chisholm Trail Community Center in Tarrant County, Texas, spilled into the parking with just an hour before polls were set to close. 
 Latoya Williams said she had waited an hour to vote there and might not have made it if her employer hadn't offered her time off. “I thought it was gonna be longer because I was being told the lines were long,” she said. 
 Williams said she was voting because “we need a change,” but also because she wants a better future for her child. 
 Voting lines spilled into the parking lot of the Chisholm Trail Community Center in Tarrant County, Texas.   Nicolle Majette / NBC News 
 “I want him to be able to go and purchase property, and him not have to worry about literally spending his life savings on a property that he probably should be owning,” she said.
 Voting is one way to make that change happen, Williams added. “The only way to make changes is to go out and vote,” she said. “No matter how many people say your vote doesn’t matter ... it’s not going to matter if you don’t get your ass out there and do something about it.”

 35m ago / 8:59 PM EST Democratic Senate nominee Josh Turek said he voted for Republicans today 
 Iowa Democratic Senate nominee Josh Turek, who has branded himself as a moderate, voted this morning in Council Bluffs, Iowa and told reporters afterwards that he voted for multiple Republicans, including a candidate for the county board of supervisors. 
 Turek is locked in a tight race against Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson with Democrats eyeing Iowa as a potential flip opportunity. Iowa Republican Sen. Joni Ernst is not seeking re-election, making it a race for an open seat.
 Trump traveled to Iowa twice in the last month to rally GOP voters in a state he won in 2024 by 13 percentage points .

 36m ago / 8:58 PM EST NBC News Exit Poll in Florida: Sen. Ashley Moody wins with support from conservatives and white voters 
 Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., edged out Democrat Angie Nixon with strong support from conservatives and white voters in the state, according to early results from the NBC News Exit Poll . 
 In addition to receiving solid backing from 93% of Republican voters, Moody also won 91% of conservatives and 60% of white voters in Florida. A majority of Latinos cast their votes for Nixon (56%). But among Latinos there was a sharp divide: 58% of Cubans supported Moody, while 68% of Puerto Ricans supported Nixon.
 Other groups backing Moody include 62% of residents who have lived in the state for 1 to 6 years, 62% of voters in small towns and rural areas, 57% of voters age 45 and older and 55% with no college degree.
 Nixon did especially well with voters under age 45 (66%), moderates (62%), independents (58%) and voters in urban areas (55%).
 44m ago / 8:50 PM EST Gerrymandering might backfire on Republicans 
 Some of the districts that were drawn in Florida for Republicans have actually been won by Democrats and it does appear, at least in House races so far, that there is a trend line emerging. 
 In general, states do not mess with their districts except for in a 10-year window after a census, where they get a sense of how many people live where, and they draw their districts accordingly. This mid-decade redistricting was a super controversial move that came after Trump went to governors in red states and said to them, essentially, “Draw me more districts that are Republican-friendly than they are Democratic-friendly.” 
 But there’s only a finite amount of voters. You can only move them around so much, and you have to pull those voters out of other districts to put them here. It is backfiring big time in Florida. If the trend holds in other states that were supposed to go for the GOP, this would be a massive error by Republicans.
 44m ago / 8:50 PM EST NBC News Exit Poll in New Hampshire: Chris Pappas wins Senate seat with 91% of LGBTQ vote 
 In New Hampshire, Senate candidate Chris Pappas, a Democrat, stopped former Sen. John E. Sununu from reclaiming his old seat, NBC News projects. Pappas, the first openly gay man to represent New Hampshire in Congress, won 91% of the LGBTQ vote, according to early results from the NBC News Exit Poll . He also claimed roughly two-thirds of voters under age 30 and women under age 45, and 59% of independents.
 46m ago / 8:48 PM EST Stock futures sell off amid strong Democratic showing in early vote counts 
 As vote tallies roll in, stock futures are falling sharply. Markets are particularly watching states such as Georgia and Texas, key states for AI data centers.
 S&P 500 futures tumbled 1% and Nasdaq 100 futures slid more than 2%. The Nasdaq 100 tracks the 100 largest tech companies at the Nasdaq stock exchange. 
 In Georgia, NBC News projected that Democratic Sen. John Ossoff will win re-election. In Texas, NBC News has not yet made a projection in the race between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico.
 With data centers facing intense push back from voters nationwide, investors are worried that Democratic wins in key states for the facilities could lead to a major slowdown in building data centers, or outright bans. A slowdown in the industry could cause major problems for companies that have hundreds of billions of dollars of investments and projects in the works.
 Show more Trump and Republicans have largely allowed the industry to regulate itself so far.
 49m ago / 8:45 PM EST Jamie Ager wins North Carolina's 11th Congressional District, NBC News projects, a gain for House Democrats 
 Democrat Jamie Ager has defeated Republican Jennifer Balkcom to win North Carolina's 11th Congressional District, NBC News projects.
 See the latest results here. 
 49m ago / 8:45 PM EST Abdul El-Sayed takes early lead in Rep. Haley Stevens' home county despite her endorsement of Mike Rogers 
 With the first substantial chunk of votes coming in to Oakland County, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is claiming an early lead over his GOP opponent, Mike Rogers. 
 Oakland County, which is the home base of Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens, who issued a shocking endorsement to Rogers over the weekend, seems to be backing El-Sayed with just under 40% of its votes counted. Of course, there are still many votes to go, but El-Sayed's advantage here indicates that he may avoid a major hit from the endorsement. 
 Key Michigan county shows El-Sayed lead as polls close 01:55 
 The county has voted for Democrats in the past, with former Vice President Kamala Harris winning Oakland with a little bit more than 10 points in 2024, which was a disappointing number for Democrats here to win statewide in Michigan. They want to usually get this number more up into the mid-teens, and I think this area is a real interesting bellwether for El-Sayed.
 Show more There's combination of the fact that this is Stevens' backyard, the fact that there’s been so much attention to the politics of the Middle East in this race, and that there’s a substantial Jewish population in Oakland County, probably the largest population of any county in Michigan.
 It tends to be a very Democratic vote, and one of the questions coming into this was if that Democratic vote, especially the Jewish Democratic vote in Oakland County, was going to stay away from El-Sayed. 
 Now this is not definitive, although we’re up to about 40% of the vote in Oakland County and the El-Sayed advantage here is much more in line with what Democrats in any given election want to be seeing out of Oakland County. 
 50m ago / 8:44 PM EST A new generation heads to the polls in Texas 
 For 18-year-old Texas resident Daniel Johnson-Baker, voting in his first election was about more than casting a ballot. It was about making sure his voice was heard, especially after his university removed polling locations from campus, making it harder for students to vote.
 “If they’re doing that, then I gotta vote,” he said. “I felt good knowing that I can finally make an impact.”
 Johnson-Baker said voting also carries a personal meaning for his family. His great-grandmother wasn’t able to vote, and his father reminded him that generations before him fought for that right. “Use your right that you got, you earned as a Black man,” he recalled his father telling him.
 Show more In Tarrant County, 19-year-old Tremaine Smith said casting his first ballot felt “different” and “kind of refreshing.” Before he was old enough to vote, he said, he could share his opinions online, but felt that didn’t always make much of a difference. “But even just voting here feels like I have a lot more power than before,” he said.
 And for 21-year-old Texan Quentin Bradfield, the motivation came down to wanting change in his community, starting with the cost of housing. “I can’t even afford a decent apartment,” he said. He also sees voting as a responsibility to the generations coming up behind him, saying he wants to help make change “not just for myself, but also the younger generation, kind of carrying the torch of the older ones left for us.”

 54m ago / 8:40 PM EST Melania Trump and other family not with POTUS tonight 
 The president's family members are not with him this evening as he follows the election from the White House, a senior administration official tells NBC News. Trump is watching the returns with Cabinet officials and staff.
 First lady Melania Trump's team had already told NBC News that she would not be there tonight and is fully focused on Russia and Ukraine talks.
 56m ago / 8:39 PM EST NBC News Exit Poll in North Carolina: Roy Cooper wins Senate seat by outperforming Trump among key groups 
 Former North Carolina Gov. Roy Cooper flipped a Senate seat for Democrats by improving on Trump's 2024 performance in the state among key groups, according to NBC News projections and the NBC News Exit Poll . Trump carried North Carolina in the three previous presidential elections. 
 Cooper made major gains among the state’s youngest voters (garnering 80% support among those age 18-24), far better than Trump’s 2024 performance among this age group (50%). Cooper also ran stronger among Latino voters (at 67% support) than Trump did (50%). And Cooper outperformed Trump’s 2024 numbers among independents and parents with children under 18.
 North Carolina’s Senate seat opened up after two-term Republican Sen. Thom Tillis dropped his re-election bid following a public disagreement with Trump.

 Republican Shelley Moore Capito has defeated Democrat Rachel Fetty Anderson to win another term in the West Virginia Senate race, NBC News projects.

 58m ago / 8:37 PM EST Karoline Leavitt, former Trump press secretary, says president is 'cautiously optimistic' 
 The former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, appearing on Fox News as an on-air analyst, said she spoke to Trump tonight and characterized the president’s midterms outlook as “cautiously optimistic.”
 “It is still very early in the night. I’ve just talked to the president. He remains cautiously optimistic. One thing he said is, he left it all on the field, and that’s certainly true,” Leavitt said, highlighting Trump’s recent campaign blitz.
 "Look, the reality of the night -- while the president and the team at the White House remain cautiously optimistic — is that history is not on his side," Leavitt added. "President Trump has been pretty pragmatic about that throughout the course of this campaign."

 2h ago / 8:29 PM EST James Talarico takes early lead in critical Texas county 
 Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico is taking a lead by 9 points in Denton County, which is essentially a mirror image of the state of Texas. 
 Denton County has more than a million people, and it's the perfect bellwether county. I think Talarico needs to win here if he's going to have a chance tonight against GOP candidate Ken Paxton. 
 Talarico leads in key Texas counties as polls close 01:30 
 Now, while the early vote tends to favor Democrats across the country, that's not necessarily the case in Texas, as typically there has not been a big shift between early votes and Election Day votes. 
 That doesn't mean there won't be a big difference tonight, but anything remotely like this out of Denton for Talarico when you get to 100% of the vote is what Democrats have been wishing to see from a place like this for decades now. 
 2h ago / 8:28 PM EST Republican John Sununu concedes New Hampshire Senate race to Democrat Chris Pappas
